POSTPONED PROCEEDINGS - At the conclusion of debate on H.J. Res. 42, the Chair put the question on passage of the joint resolution and by voice vote, announced that the ayes had prevailed. Mr. Pallone demanded the yeas and nays and the Chair postponed further proceedings until a time to be announced.
The previous question was ordered pursuant to the rule.
DEBATE - The House proceeded with one hour of debate on H.J. Res. 42.

dimensions.assessment: Affects manufacturers, distributors, and sellers of specific consumer and commercial appliances such as washing machines and air conditioners.
dimensions.evidence: consumer products (e.g., washing machines and dishwashers) and industrial equipment (e.g., computer room air conditioners).

dimensions.assessment: Alters regulatory, reporting, and labeling requirements for businesses rather than direct life-changing impacts on individuals.
dimensions.evidence: eliminates new, more stringent certification, labeling, and enforcement requirements related to energy conservation standards

dimensions.assessment: Changes regulatory compliance burdens and reporting procedures for industry, but federal budgetary spending amounts are not specified.
Nullifies a specific agency rule under the Congressional Review Act, invalidating a discrete set of Department of Energy regulations.
dimensions.evidence: That Congress disapproves the rule submitted by the Department of Energy... and such rule shall have no force or effect.

dimensions.assessment: Permanently eliminates the designated rule nationwide.

missing_information: Specific economic impact on manufacturers or compliance cost estimates
Detailed breakdown of how many appliance models are affected
importance_detail.rationale: This joint resolution nullifies a specific Department of Energy rule concerning appliance certification, labeling, and enforcement provisions, restoring previous requirements for certain consumer products and commercial equipment.
